phase_name: Authority Evaluation Model Implementation Contract Second Repair
summary: Phase 147E.2 repaired AEMIC-001 v1.1 to v1.2, closing BF-147F.1-1, the second, distinct Blocking finding Phase 147F.1 independently discovered. AuthorityEvaluationOutcome.template_ref and .template_version are mandatory, unconditional output fields for all three EvaluationResult branches, described as a verbatim copy of evaluate()'s own input, but evaluate()'s own frozen five-parameter signature (v1.1) never accepted template_ref or template_version as inputs; for the eligible/ineligible branches a value could be undocumentedly derived from declaration.template_ref/.template_version, but for the indeterminate branch (declaration is None) no value was reachable anywhere, making a mandatory field's construction impossible for one of exactly three closed branches evaluate() is required to support. This phase independently reproduced the defect directly from AEMIC-001 v1.1's own text before re-reading Phase 147F.1's own account a second time, re-deriving the same declaration_ref-vs-template_ref/template_version table asymmetry that phase identified. Seven candidate repair families were independently assessed against the governing prompt's own selection criteria: a new AuthorityEvaluationRequest wrapper type (rejected as disproportionate and previously already declined by AEMIC-REQ-019 itself); two direct evaluate() parameters (selected); deriving identity from EligibleAuthorityDeclaration alone (rejected, fails the indeterminate branch by definition); making the fields conditional (rejected, narrows an existing auditability guarantee); a dedicated DecisionTemplateIdentity value object (rejected as over-engineered); Registry-derived identity (rejected, inverts causality and expands Registry responsibility); and hidden or ambient lookup (rejected outright, violates forbidden-import and purity rules). The selected repair adds template_ref and template_version as evaluate()'s own first two parameters, widening the signature from five to seven, with a new deterministic verification rule (AEMIC-REQ-103) requiring evaluate() to check a resolved Declaration's own template_ref/template_version against these two new parameters whenever a Declaration is present, failing closed via a new typed exception, TemplateIdentityMismatchError, on any disagreement, ordered strictly before evaluation_result determination and citation_text enforcement (AEMIC-REQ-104/105). Every mandatory AuthorityEvaluationOutcome field now has a reachable, closed-input construction source for every one of the three EvaluationResult branches, including indeterminate -- the property BF-147F.1-1 identified as absent. EligibleAuthorityDeclaration's AEM-001-frozen six-field shape is unchanged; no new public type was introduced. AEMIC-001 is now v1.2. Section 5, Section 6 (note only), Section 10.2 (note only), Section 13.1, Section 14 (including a new Section 14.2 subsection), Section 15 (note only plus one new security-table row), Section 16 (note only), Section 18 (note only), Section 20, Section 22, and Section 23 were amended; every other section is byte-for-byte unchanged from v1.1; no requirement identifier was renumbered, reassigned, retired, or reused; five new identifiers were appended (AEMIC-REQ-103 through AEMIC-REQ-107). BF-147F-1 remains Repaired, unaffected and unreopened by this phase. F-147F.1-2 (empty-string citation), F-147F.1-3 (non-string citation typing), F-147F.1-4 (deserialization cross-field ambiguity), and the direct-construction Informational observation were each independently re-affirmed unrelated to BF-147F.1-1 and left open, exactly as the governing prompt's own scope instruction required. Overall Verdict: IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT SECOND REPAIR COMPLETE. Full detail in docs/PHASE_147E.2_AUTHORITY_EVALUATION_MODEL_IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACT_SECOND_REPAIR.md.
